title: Where Can I See Kakobuy QC Photos?
meta: Learn when Kakobuy QC photos become relevant, how to check the current item record, and how to separate warehouse images from listing photos.
targetKeyword: where to see Kakobuy QC photos
quickAnswer: Kakobuy QC photos become relevant after an item reaches the warehouse stage. Kakobuy's public homepage says goods are checked and weighed after arrival at its warehouse, and the result is fed back to the user. To find photos for your item, start from the exact item, order, or warehouse record in the live Kakobuy interface. The current interface can vary, so follow the record you see in your own account.
body:
## Why This Matters

People often find product links, spreadsheets, and screenshots before they understand where item-specific photos appear. That creates confusion. A seller image, a spreadsheet image, and a warehouse image can all show the same product type, but they do not prove the same thing.

The useful question is not only “where are the photos?” It is also whether those photos belong to the exact item you are checking. Keep menu labels, photo counts, timing, and extra-photo options tied to the live item record instead of an old screenshot.

## First Separate the Image Types

Seller listing photos show how a product is presented before a specific item reaches a warehouse. They may show colors, sizes, packaging, or design details. They are useful for product discovery, but they are not tied to your received item.

Product research images organize visible product details beside price references, SKU choices, size labels, and source links. These images help you prepare before you open a third-party platform. They should not be described as Kakobuy warehouse QC photos unless the page clearly identifies them that way.

Warehouse QC photos should be connected to a received item record. They are most useful when you can match the image set to the item, option, and stage you are reviewing.

## When the Photos Become Relevant

Kakobuy's current public homepage describes a flow where goods reach Kakobuy's warehouse and then go through checking and weighing. That supports one careful statement: warehouse inspection is connected to the warehouse-arrival stage.

That does not prove a fixed public menu path. It also does not prove how many photos appear, how fast they appear, or whether extra angles are available for every item.

Before you look for QC photos, check the current status shown on your item record. If the item has not reached the warehouse stage, a warehouse image set may not yet be relevant.

## How to Locate the Right Record

Start from the exact item record, not from a general gallery.

Use this order:

1. Open the current Kakobuy item, order, or warehouse record.
2. Confirm the product title or source identifier.
3. Confirm the selected color, size, style, or option.
4. Look for a photo, inspection, image, or record area connected to that item.
5. If the record is at the expected stage but no image area is visible, use Kakobuy's current support channel and provide the item reference.

Do not use an old tutorial screenshot as proof that your interface must look the same. Account state, item state, language settings, and interface updates may differ.

## What to Check in the Image Set

Start with the whole product. Confirm that the general shape, color placement, and main parts match the selected item.

Then check the details that matter for the category. For shoes, look at the toe, heel, both sides, outsole, interior label, and any size mark. For accessories, check visible hardware, shape, closure, logo placement, and interior views if shown. For electronics, check visible model marks, ports, labels, included parts, and surface condition.

Write observations as evidence, not conclusions:

- The size label is readable.
- The heel is not shown clearly.
- The color looks different under the available lighting.
- No measurement reference appears.
- The source option cannot be matched from the photo alone.

A photo can support a visual observation. It cannot prove authenticity, comfort, hidden construction, durability, or a future result.

## Compare Against the Source Record

Use the marketplace source record as a second reference point. Compare title, item identifier, option labels, listed price, seller images, and current source-page state.

This can reveal a mismatch between the item you selected and the image set you are viewing. It can also show that a spreadsheet or saved link is old.

The source page is time-sensitive. A working URL does not prove every old option, price, or image is still current. Save the item identifier and review the live source before relying on a copied label.

## Product Research Before the Warehouse Stage

Before warehouse photos are available, CuriCart can help you organize the intended product record. The [CuriCart Kakobuy product research guide](https://www.curicart.com/en/agentsView_15_6.html) brings product photos, listed-price references, selectable SKU or size data, and available Weidian source records into one research view.

Use these examples only as product research references:

- [THE ROGER Clubhouse Pro Tennis Shoes - Style 30](https://www.curicart.com/en/productview_4234_80.html?proname=on-the-roger-clubhouse-pro-tennis-shoes)
- [On Cloudmonster 1 White Gray - Style 21](https://www.curicart.com/en/productview_4203_79.html?proname=on-cloudmonster-1-running-shoes)
- [Nike Mind 001 Flyknit QS Slides - Style 16](https://www.curicart.com/en/productview_4160_77.html?proname=nike-slides-sandals)

These pages are not Kakobuy warehouse records. Use them to practise comparing photos, options, prices, and source context before you review a live item record.

## Related Product Research Categories

Use category cards on the page for related CuriCart research:

- Shoe product research: best fit for this page.
- Accessories product research: useful for checking visual details and option labels.
- Electronics product research: useful when the same photo-checking method applies to visible model and part details.

## Common Mistakes

The first mistake is treating every product image as a QC photo. Check the source of the image first.

The second mistake is reviewing a photo without matching it to an item record. Similar product names are not enough.

The third mistake is assuming photos can prove authenticity or long-term quality. They cannot.

The fourth mistake is using another user's screenshot as a universal menu guide. Interfaces and item states can differ.

The fifth mistake is skipping the live source page. A spreadsheet row or saved label can be stale.

faq.question: Where can I see Kakobuy QC photos?
faq.answer: Check the current item, order, or warehouse record after the item reaches the warehouse stage. Kakobuy's public homepage says items are checked and weighed after warehouse arrival, but the account interface can vary. Use the item record you see now.

faq.question: Are seller photos the same as Kakobuy QC photos?
faq.answer: No. Seller photos show a listing. Warehouse QC photos should be tied to a specific received item record.

faq.question: Why might I not see photos yet?
faq.answer: The item may not be at the relevant stage, you may be viewing the wrong record, or the current interface may place images in a different area. Check the item identifier and status first.

faq.question: What details should I check first?
faq.answer: Confirm the item, option, color, size, and visible labels. Then review main surfaces, key details, and any measurement or label shown.

faq.question: Can QC photos prove authenticity?
faq.answer: No. Photos can show visible details. They cannot prove authenticity, hidden construction, comfort, durability, or fit.

title: Why Is My Kakobuy Product Link Not Working?
meta: Diagnose a Kakobuy product link that does not load. Check the full source URL, item identifier, live source page, options, and current message.
quickAnswer: When a Kakobuy product link is not working, test the original marketplace source URL first. Confirm that the link begins with `http://` or `https://`, contains the expected item identifier, and opens at the original destination. Then compare Kakobuy's current message or manual-entry page with the live source page. Do not assume one cause from the error alone.
body:
## Why This Matters

Users often paste a product link and expect one clear result. When the result fails, they may not know whether the problem is the source page, the copied URL, the platform parser, a region or login state, or a changed item record.

A failed product link can have several causes. The safest approach is to separate the original source URL from the Kakobuy result page and then compare both records.

## Start With the Exact Message

Write down what you see before changing the link. A blank page, redirect, manual-entry form, upload field, reload prompt, or source-page error are different problems.

Current Kakobuy pages can show a manual product form when the system cannot directly read a product URL or when a third-party link needs manual information. The rendered page reviewed for this guide asked for product information such as product link, name, specification, product image, note, unit price, quantity, and domestic shipping. It also told users to confirm third-party product information carefully.

That interface does not prove why your link failed. It tells you to verify the source and provide cleaner product information.

## Check Whether the URL Is Complete

A product name is not a product link. A screenshot is not a product link. A shortened label in a chat is not always the full destination.

Paste the link into a plain text field and inspect it. It should include:

- `http://` or `https://`
- The marketplace domain
- The product path
- The source item identifier when visible
- Any parameters needed to open the same item

For Weidian, look for `itemID=` followed by digits. Preserve the full URL until you know which parameters are optional.

## Open the Original Source Separately

Test the marketplace URL outside Kakobuy. This separates a source-page problem from a Kakobuy-reading problem.

Record what happens:

1. The source page opens and shows the expected item.
2. The source opens but shows a different item or option.
3. The source redirects to login, verification, or another page.
4. The source returns an error or unavailable-item notice.
5. The source page only partly loads.

Do not treat all five outcomes as “dead link.” If the source opens correctly while Kakobuy shows a manual-entry page or error, save both records. If the source itself no longer presents the item, an old spreadsheet label cannot restore it.

## Match the Item Identifier

Product titles are weak identifiers. Sellers, spreadsheet editors, and social posts may use short names, translated names, or labels shared by many items.

For Weidian links, record the `itemID`. Compare it character by character.

Current CuriCart examples show why this matters:

- [THE ROGER Style 30 record](https://www.curicart.com/en/productview_4234_80.html?proname=on-the-roger-clubhouse-pro-tennis-shoes) points to Weidian itemID `7805795543`.
- [Cloudmonster Style 21 record](https://www.curicart.com/en/productview_4203_79.html?proname=on-cloudmonster-1-running-shoes) points to Weidian itemID `7808777696`.
- [Nike Mind Style 16 record](https://www.curicart.com/en/productview_4160_77.html?proname=nike-slides-sandals) points to Weidian itemID `7805487415`.

Each number identifies a different source record. A correct-looking product name cannot replace that check.

## Compare the Product Context

A link can load and still be wrong for your purpose. Compare the current source page with the record that led you there.

Check:

- Product title or recognizable model wording.
- Main product images.
- Listed-price context.
- Available style, color, or size labels.
- Seller or store context when visible.
- Source item identifier.

If the itemID matches but the visible content has changed, record the mismatch. A seller can change listing content, options can disappear, and cached previews can outlive the page they describe.

## Treat Link Converters as an Extra Layer

A converter can wrap or rewrite a destination. It does not replace the original source record.

When a converted link fails, return to the marketplace URL and item identifier. Check whether the converter preserved the full destination. Do not pass a link through several converters in a row, because each wrapper makes the source harder to audit.

Keep two values in your notes:

- The original marketplace URL.
- The Kakobuy result or manual-entry URL.

If one fails later, the other helps you identify where the failure occurred.

## Use a Controlled Retry

Retry only after you save the original evidence.

Use this sequence:

1. Copy the original source URL again.
2. Confirm that it starts with `http://` or `https://`.
3. Open it directly and verify the item identifier.
4. Enter the unchanged full URL in Kakobuy.
5. Read the current message or form state.
6. If the source is valid but Kakobuy still cannot read it, use the current manual-entry or support option shown in the interface.

Do not invent a replacement itemID. Do not remove unfamiliar parameters at random. A shortened URL may load, but it may also lose information needed to identify the intended page.

## Research the Product Before Retrying

The [CuriCart Kakobuy guide](https://www.curicart.com/en/agentsView_15_6.html) helps you compare product photos, style or size options, listed-price references, and available Weidian source links. This can confirm whether the source record you copied matches the product you intended to inspect.

You can also start from the [CuriCart Kakobuy topic page](https://www.curicart.com/en/agentslist_6.html?spreadsheet=Kakobuy) when you need the current guide entry rather than an old saved label.

CuriCart cannot diagnose a private Kakobuy account error. Its value here is source comparison: product name, visible images, option labels, and itemID can be checked before you retry the source URL.

## Related Product Research Categories

Use category cards on the page for related CuriCart research:

- Shoe product research: strongest relevance because the verified examples are footwear.
- Accessories product research: useful when link checks involve visual option labels or small-item details.
- Electronics product research: useful when model marks, ports, and included parts help confirm the source record.

## Common Mistakes

The first mistake is treating a product title as a link. A title may help you search, but it does not carry the source identifier.

The second is testing only the Kakobuy result. Always test the original marketplace destination separately.

The third is using an old spreadsheet row without checking the live source. A spreadsheet can preserve a useful record, but its link and labels are time-sensitive.

The fourth is assigning one cause too early. A temporary issue, source change, parser problem, login redirect, or incomplete URL can look similar.

The fifth is accepting the first page that loads. A working URL is useful only when its item identifier and product context match the intended record.

faq.question: Why is my Kakobuy product link not working?
faq.answer: The exact cause cannot be known from the failure alone. Check the complete source URL, the item identifier, the current source page, and the current Kakobuy message or manual-entry state.

faq.question: What format should a Kakobuy product link use?
faq.answer: Use the complete marketplace URL. It should begin with `http://` or `https://` and include the path and identifier needed to open the source item.

faq.question: How do I check a Weidian itemID?
faq.answer: Find `itemID=` in the source URL and save the digits that follow it. Compare that number with the product record you intended to open.

faq.question: Does a working link mean the product details are current?
faq.answer: No. A page can load while options, price, images, or seller context have changed. Review the live source content each time.

faq.question: What should I send to support?
faq.answer: Provide the original source URL, item identifier, current Kakobuy message, screenshot, and check time. This gives support a specific record instead of a general description.

title: How to Choose a Kakobuy Spreadsheet With QC Photos
meta: Use a practical checklist to assess a Kakobuy spreadsheet with QC photos, source links, item IDs, options, image context, and update clues.
quickAnswer: Choose a Kakobuy spreadsheet with QC photos by checking row-level evidence, not the size of the list. A useful row identifies the product, preserves the original source URL and item identifier, labels the image type, shows the relevant option, and gives a current-status clue. Open the live source page before relying on price, SKU, size, or photo coverage.
body:
## Why This Matters

Many Kakobuy spreadsheet pages promise large lists, updated finds, or QC photos. The problem is that a spreadsheet can look useful even when the row-level evidence is weak.

A good spreadsheet helps you narrow research. A weak spreadsheet can hide broken links, old labels, unclear image sources, and mismatched options. Treat the spreadsheet as a starting point, then verify the row you want to use.

## A Spreadsheet Is an Index, Not Proof

A spreadsheet can reduce search time. It does not make every row current, complete, or accurate.

Large row counts are not a quality measure by themselves. A list can contain duplicates, old source pages, broad product labels, missing options, or images with no clear origin. A smaller sheet with traceable rows can be more useful than a large sheet with promotional labels.

Judge the spreadsheet at row level. Select several rows from different sections and test whether each one answers the same basic questions.

## Check Product Identity First

Each row should make the product easy to identify.

Look for:

- A specific product name.
- A clear category.
- A style, color, model, or option label.
- The original source URL.
- A visible item identifier when the source supports one.

A label such as “popular shoes” is weak. It may point to many products. It is also hard to compare with a live source page.

For Weidian, record the numeric `itemID`. Do not confuse a spreadsheet row number with a marketplace item identifier.

## Identify What the Photos Are

The phrase “QC photos” is often used loosely. A spreadsheet should explain the origin of its images.

Seller listing photos show how the product is presented by the seller. Product research images may organize listing photos beside SKU and source information. Community images may show another user's item. Warehouse QC photos should be connected to a particular received item or record.

Do not classify an image only by its background. A plain table, ruler, or storage setting does not prove image origin.

Ask these questions:

1. Is the image source named?
2. Is the item identifier visible nearby?
3. Does the image match the selected option?
4. Is there a date, record label, or current-status clue?
5. Does the image link still open?

If the answers are missing, the image may still help with visual research. It should not be treated as the QC record for your own item.

## Compare Photos With the Selected Option

One source listing can include many colors, sizes, or styles. A spreadsheet row must make the selected option clear.

Compare the spreadsheet label with the live page. Check color placement, shape, visible labels, included parts, and style wording. For shoes, compare the side profile, heel, toe, outsole, and visible size label. For accessories, compare closures, shape, hardware, and visible tags. For electronics, compare ports, model labels, color, and included parts.

Record missing evidence instead of guessing. If the row says “black” but the linked photos show several colors with no selected option, mark the option as not confirmed.

## Verify the Source Link

Every useful row should preserve the original marketplace source URL. A wrapped or converted link can be convenient, but the source record is needed for auditing.

Open the source separately and confirm:

- The destination loads.
- The item identifier matches.
- The product context is recognizable.
- The relevant option still appears.
- The listed price is shown as a reference.
- Seller or store context is visible when available.

If the source has changed, the spreadsheet row needs a new check. Do not rely on “updated” text unless the row shows what was tested and when.

## Review Price, SKU, and Size Separately

Price, SKU, and size should not be collapsed into one “details” field.

A listed price is a reference captured from a page. It may not reflect every option or a later page state. A SKU label identifies a choice, but it does not prove the choice is currently available. A size label can show the seller's mapping, but it does not prove fit.

A strong spreadsheet preserves the visible wording instead of silently converting it. If a row changes EU, US, UK, JP, or CM labels, it should identify the source of that conversion.

Use “unknown” when a field is absent. Empty information is safer than a confident guess.

## Test Several Rows Before Trusting the Layout

Do not judge a spreadsheet from its first screen.

Test several rows and score each one:

1. Product identity is specific.
2. Original source URL is preserved.
3. Item identifier matches the live page.
4. Image type and selected option are clear.
5. Price, SKU, and size fields keep their source context.
6. Missing or time-sensitive details are marked.

This score is a research aid. A row that passes today can still change later.

## Product Research Examples

The [CuriCart Kakobuy guide](https://www.curicart.com/en/agentsView_15_6.html) provides current product-research examples. These examples keep photos, options, price references, and source context together without treating every image as warehouse QC.

- [THE ROGER Style 30 product record](https://www.curicart.com/en/productview_4234_80.html?proname=on-the-roger-clubhouse-pro-tennis-shoes) includes product photos, option labels, a listed-price reference, and Weidian itemID `7805795543`.
- [Cloudmonster Style 21 product record](https://www.curicart.com/en/productview_4203_79.html?proname=on-cloudmonster-1-running-shoes) includes product photos, a shoe-size selector, a listed-price reference, and Weidian itemID `7808777696`.
- [Nike Mind Style 16 product record](https://www.curicart.com/en/productview_4160_77.html?proname=nike-slides-sandals) includes product photos, style and shoe-size selectors, a listed-price reference, and Weidian itemID `7805487415`.

Use these records as examples of how to keep product, option, image, and source context together. Recheck every live page before relying on it.

## Related Product Research Categories

Use category cards on the page for related CuriCart research:

- Shoe product research: highest relevance for Kakobuy spreadsheet rows about footwear.
- Accessories product research: useful when spreadsheet rows include bags, glasses, or small items.
- Electronics product research: useful for rows where visible model marks, ports, and included parts matter.

## Red Flags

Be cautious when a spreadsheet uses big claims but gives little evidence.

Warning signs include:

- Images with no source label.
- Converted links with no original marketplace URL.
- Product names that are too broad.
- One price shown without an option or check date.
- Size conversions with no visible source.
- Repeated rows pointing to the same item identifier.
- “Updated” labels that do not identify what changed.
- Photos that do not match the selected style.

A good spreadsheet makes uncertainty visible. If missing fields are hidden behind promotional wording, the sheet is hard to audit.

faq.question: What should a Kakobuy spreadsheet with QC photos include?
faq.answer: It should identify the product, preserve the original source URL and item identifier, label the image type, connect images to an option, and show price, SKU, or size context when available.

faq.question: Are all photos in a Kakobuy spreadsheet warehouse QC photos?
faq.answer: No. They may be seller images, product research photos, community uploads, or warehouse records. Check the source and item connection before classifying them.

faq.question: How can I tell whether a spreadsheet link is current?
faq.answer: Open the original marketplace destination, compare the item identifier and product context, and note the current page state. An “updated” label alone is not enough.

faq.question: Does a large spreadsheet mean better product coverage?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. Row count does not show whether links work, images are traceable, options match, or records are current.

faq.question: Can spreadsheet QC photos confirm product quality?
faq.answer: They can support visual observations about details that are shown. They cannot establish hidden construction, fit, durability, authenticity, or what another physical item currently looks like.

title: How to Read a Kakobuy Weidian Link Before Using It
h1: How to Read a Kakobuy Weidian Link Before Using It
meta: Learn how to check a Kakobuy Weidian link by reading the source URL, itemID, product photos, listed price, SKU, and size-style details.
quickAnswer: A Kakobuy Weidian link should be read as a source record first. Start with the full URL and the numeric itemID. Then compare the product title, product photos, listed price, SKU, size, color, and style details against the page you plan to use. A link alone does not confirm the current option, final price, product status, or seller response.
body:
## Why This Matters

Many Kakobuy searches start with a single Weidian link. That link can look simple, but it often carries several pieces of information.

The most useful part is usually the itemID. It helps you keep the original source page separate from screenshots, copied titles, spreadsheet rows, and short labels.

The problem is that a link is not the same as a complete product record. A product page may show one title, several photos, a listed price, and a group of size or style choices. Those fields can change. Some fields may also be missing when you compare the same item on another page.

So the safer research step is simple. Read the Weidian link first. Then compare it with the visible product information before you continue anywhere else.

## Start With the Full Source URL

Do not rely only on a screenshot, a spreadsheet row, or a copied product title.

Save the full source URL first. A Weidian source URL may include this kind of item identifier:

`itemID=7805795543`

The number after `itemID=` is important. It gives you a stable reference point when titles or preview text are short.

For example, a CuriCart product page for THE ROGER Clubhouse Pro Tennis Shoes - Style 30 currently shows Weidian itemID `7805795543`. That itemID is a useful record to compare with the original source page.

Do the same check before you use any product link. Keep the original URL until you have finished comparing the title, photos, listed price, and options.

## Check the Product Title and Style Name

The product title should be your first visible clue.

Look for the brand or product name, the model name, the color phrase, and the style number if one is shown. Do not assume a short spreadsheet label includes all of that detail.

A clear product record should help you answer these questions:

- What product is this page showing?
- Is the model name visible?
- Is a style, color, or version label visible?
- Does the title match the product photos?
- Does the title match the source page you are checking?

CuriCart examples show why this matters. THE ROGER Clubhouse Pro Tennis Shoes - Style 30, On Cloudmonster 1 Men's Cushioned Everyday Shoe White Gray - Style 21, and Nike Mind 001 Flyknit QS Slides - Black Orange Gradient Style 16 all carry product names and style labels. Those labels make the product easier to compare than a bare link.

## Compare Product Photos Before You Continue

Product photos can help you compare visible details. They can show shape, color, sole design, texture, logo placement, and other visible features.

Do not treat every product photo as a warehouse QC photo. A product image, a seller image, a CuriCart product image, and an agent-issued warehouse image can be different kinds of images.

For a Weidian link, use photos to answer practical questions:

- Does the photo match the product title?
- Do different photos show the same item?
- Are the color and style details visible?
- Are important parts hidden, cropped, or unclear?
- Is there enough visual detail to compare the option you plan to choose?

If the photos are too limited, record that as unknown. Do not fill in missing details from memory.

## Read the Listed Price as a Reference

A listed price can help you compare records, but it should not be treated as the final price you will pay.

Use the listed price as a reference field. It can help you check whether two pages are likely talking about the same item. It can also help you notice if a copied row and the source page do not match.

But a listed price may not include every cost. It may also change on the source page. Do not use it as proof of a final total.

In the current CuriCart examples, the product pages show listed price references next to other product details. These values are useful for comparing visible records. They should still be checked again on the live source page before any decision.

## Check SKU, Size, Color, and Style Options

The option section is often where mistakes happen.

The source page may have size choices, color choices, style choices, or other SKU labels. A copied link may not show which option someone meant. A spreadsheet row may also simplify the option field.

Check the option labels one by one:

- Size label
- Color label
- Style number
- Version name
- Any option note on the page

For shoe examples, the visible size labels can matter a lot. A CuriCart page may show EU, US, UK, or CM values. Those labels should stay separate. Do not merge them into one size unless the page itself clearly supports that comparison.

If the source page has several options, write down the exact option you are checking.

## Keep Source Page Context Separate

A Weidian link is only one layer of the research record.

Keep these parts separate:

- The source URL
- The itemID
- The product title
- The product photos
- The listed price
- The SKU or size-style option
- The page where you found the link

This helps when you compare the same product across a guide, a spreadsheet, a CuriCart product page, and the live source page.

It also helps you avoid a common mistake: treating a link as if it already proves the exact product option. It does not. It points to a source record that still needs to be checked.

## Common Mistakes

One common mistake is using only the copied product name. A copied name can lose the itemID, option labels, and source-page context.

Another mistake is reading the first photo as the selected option. Some product pages show shared photos for several options. Check whether the option label supports what you think the image shows.

A third mistake is treating listed price as final price. Use it as a comparison field, not as a final total.

A fourth mistake is mixing product photos with warehouse QC photos. They can serve different purposes.

A fifth mistake is removing unfamiliar URL parameters too early. Keep the original link until the source record has been checked.

## Related Product Research on CuriCart

These examples can help you practise reading source records, photos, listed price references, and size-style details:

- [THE ROGER Clubhouse Pro Tennis Shoes - Style 30](https://www.curicart.com/en/productview_4234_80.html?proname=on-the-roger-clubhouse-pro-tennis-shoes)
- [On Cloudmonster 1 Men's Cushioned Everyday Shoe White Gray - Style 21](https://www.curicart.com/en/productview_4203_79.html?proname=on-cloudmonster-1-running-shoes)
- [Nike Mind 001 Flyknit QS Slides - Black Orange Gradient Style 16](https://www.curicart.com/en/productview_4160_77.html?proname=nike-slides-sandals)
- [Shoe product research](https://www.curicart.com/en/Productlistt_1.html?fuid=1&&category=Shoe)
- [Kakobuy product link and QC photo guide](https://www.curicart.com/en/agentsView_15_6.html)

faq.question: What is the most important part of a Kakobuy Weidian link?
faq.answer: The full source URL is the most important part to save first. If a numeric itemID is present, save that too. These details help you compare the original source page with a product guide, spreadsheet row, or product research page.

faq.question: Can a Weidian link confirm the exact product option?
faq.answer: Not by itself. The link may point to a product record, but you still need to check the visible title, photos, listed price, and SKU or size-style option.

faq.question: Should I remove extra URL parameters?
faq.answer: Do not remove parts of the URL until you have saved the original source link. Some parameters may not matter, but deleting them too early can make later comparison harder.

faq.question: Are product photos the same as Kakobuy QC photos?

title: Kakobuy Shoe Size Chart and Labels Guide
h1: How to Read a Kakobuy Shoe Size Chart and Labels
meta: Compare Kakobuy shoe size labels by checking EU, US, UK, and CM fields, seller size context, product photos, and SKU options before choosing.
quickAnswer: Read Kakobuy shoe size labels as option labels, not as a fit promise. Compare EU, US, UK, and CM values exactly as shown. Then check the product title, photos, SKU option, seller size context, and any visible chart before choosing. If a field is missing or unclear, keep it unknown instead of guessing.
body:
## Why This Matters

Shoe size searches often look simple. A page may show EU, US, UK, or CM labels beside each option. But those labels are not always the same kind of information.

One field may be a product option. Another may be a brand label. Another may be a seller size chart. A measurement photo or warehouse note would be another kind of record.

If you mix those records together, you can choose the wrong option. The safer method is to keep each field separate and compare the visible labels before you continue.

This guide focuses on visible shoe size labels and product research context. It does not promise that a size will fit.

## Separate the Size Label From the Size Chart

A size label is usually the option you select. It may look like EU40, US8.5, UK6.5, or CM25.

A size chart is different. It may explain how a seller or brand maps sizes to foot length, insole length, or another measurement.

Do not treat an option label as a full size chart. Also do not treat a size chart as proof that a specific pair will fit.

Keep these records separate:

- SKU size label
- Seller or source-page size chart
- Product title or model name
- Product photos
- Brand sizing reference
- Any measurement image or note

If the page only shows option labels, write down only those labels. Do not invent missing measurements.

## Read EU, US, UK, and CM Fields Carefully

Different pages may show different size systems.

The current CuriCart shoe examples show why this matters.

THE ROGER Clubhouse Pro Tennis Shoes - Style 30 currently shows EU, US, and UK labels. Examples include EU36 / US5 / UK3 and EU40 / US8.5 / UK6.5.

On Cloudmonster 1 Men's Cushioned Everyday Shoe White Gray - Style 21 also shows EU, US, and UK labels. The visible labels include half sizes such as EU36.5 / US5.5 / UK3.5.

Nike Mind 001 Flyknit QS Slides - Black Orange Gradient Style 16 shows EU, US, UK, and CM labels. Examples include EU36 / US4 / UK3.5 / CM23 and EU44 / US10 / UK9 / CM28.

These fields should not be collapsed into one value. Read each label as it appears.

## Do Not Treat CM as a Fit Guarantee

CM can look more precise than EU, US, or UK. That does not make it a fit promise.

A CM value may be a label, a brand field, a foot-length reference, an insole reference, or another sizing convention depending on the page. The page has to show what the value means.

If the page only shows `CM23`, record it as `CM23`. Do not automatically call it foot length, insole length, or exact measurement unless the page clearly says so.

This small distinction matters. A user may see the same size number on two pages but the pages may not use the same sizing context.

## Compare the Size Label With the Product Title

Before choosing a size, confirm that the title and option labels belong to the same product.

Check the model name first. Then check the style number, color phrase, and product type.

For example, a product title like On Cloudmonster 1 Men's Cushioned Everyday Shoe White Gray - Style 21 gives more context than a short row that only says "Cloudmonster."

The title does not prove fit. But it helps you avoid comparing the wrong model or style.

## Compare the Size Label With Product Photos

Photos cannot tell you exact fit. They can still help you check visible product context.

Use photos to confirm:

- The product type is correct.
- The color matches the selected style.
- The sole shape and upper design match the title.
- The photos show the same product across the page.
- There are enough visual details to compare the selected option.

Do not use photos to guess a size if the size label is missing. If you cannot see the size option, record it as unknown.

## Watch for Half Sizes and Missing Systems

Half sizes are easy to miss.

EU36 and EU36.5 are not the same label. US8 and US8.5 are not the same label. UK6 and UK6.5 are not the same label.

Missing systems can also create confusion. One product may show EU/US/UK only. Another may show EU/US/UK/CM. Do not add a missing CM value yourself.

If you need a comparison across systems, use a source that clearly explains the mapping. If you do not have that source, keep the comparison open.

## Build a Simple Size Record

Before you continue, write down the size record in a simple format:

- Product title
- Source URL or itemID
- Selected SKU label
- EU label if shown
- US label if shown
- UK label if shown
- CM label if shown
- Color or style label
- Any visible seller size chart note

This keeps your research organized. It also makes it easier to compare a CuriCart product page, a source page, and any other page you plan to check.

## Common Mistakes

One mistake is choosing a size from memory. Always check the current visible option label.

Another mistake is assuming CM always means the same measurement. It does not unless the page explains it.

A third mistake is ignoring half sizes. Small differences in labels can change the selected option.

A fourth mistake is comparing two models as if they use the same size context. Different products can display labels differently.

A fifth mistake is treating photos as measurement proof. Photos can help compare visible details, but they do not replace a size chart or a measurement record.

## Related Product Research on CuriCart

These product and category pages can help you practise comparing visible shoe labels and product context:

- [THE ROGER Clubhouse Pro Tennis Shoes - Style 30](https://www.curicart.com/en/productview_4234_80.html?proname=on-the-roger-clubhouse-pro-tennis-shoes)

faq.question: Is a Kakobuy shoe size label the same as a size chart?
faq.answer: No. A size label is the option shown on the product page. A size chart explains how sizes may map to measurements. A product can show one without clearly showing the other.

faq.question: Can I convert EU, US, UK, and CM labels myself?
faq.answer: Do not guess a conversion. Record each visible label as shown. Use a reliable chart only when the page or brand source clearly supports the comparison.

faq.question: Does CM always mean foot length?
faq.answer: No. CM should not be treated as foot length unless the page says that. It may be a label or another sizing reference. Keep the exact wording.

faq.question: What should I do if the size chart is missing?
faq.answer: Record the size label that is visible and mark the missing chart as unknown. Do not fill in measurements from another product unless there is a clear source for that comparison.

faq.question: Can product photos prove the size?
faq.answer: No. Product photos can help compare visible details, but they cannot prove the selected size or fit. Use photos together with the visible SKU and size labels.
